newsitem.title: USA: Container ship refloated from Florida coral reef.
newsitem.headline: Container ship refloated from Florida coral reef.

text.p: Salvage experts successfully floated the 600-foot (182 metre) container ship Houston off a patch of sand and coral where it had been stuck for nearly six days, a Coast Guard Spokesman said late on Saturday.
None of the freighter's 810,000 gallons (3.06 million litres) of fuel was spilled, according to the Coast Guard.

The ship, which ran aground 13 miles (20 km) southeast of Key West in the Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary, was being towed to a safe anchorage site less than two miles (3 km) away, said Coast Guard spokesman Cmdr. Marcus Woodring.

Salvage experts pumped 540,000 gallons (2.04 million litres) of fuel into a barge on Saturday afternoon to lighten the ship's load, and the ship foated free at 8:37 p.m. (0137 GMT Sunday), just before high tide, Woodring said.
The Houston plowed into a patch of protected coral late on Sunday after an error in navigation.
Once a hull inspection was conducted, the ship was to be towed to Miami, Woodring said.
Environmentalists consider the grounding a close call for the nearby Western Sambos Ecological Reserve, which is the heart of the lower keys ecosystem.

The Houston, owned by the Mexican freight company Transportacion Maritima Mexican, violated a special no-shipping zone designed to protect the fragile coral reef area, which was covered by the rising sea millions of years ago.

While the fuel was being transferred into the barge, salvage experts were pumping seawater into the Houston's ballast area to compensate, Woodring said. The seawater was pumped out when technicians were ready to move the ship to minimize further damage to the reef.
